evidence.field: PDF page 77, printed page 65; 尔 entry
evidence.text: Directly inspected the original scan. The entry describes 尔 as a simplified form of 爾; says the construction of 爾 in oracle-bone and bronze forms is unclear; reports the earliest then-visible simplified 尔 in the Warring States Zhongshan Wang Ding; and gives a bronze inscription use as a second-person pronoun, glossed as equivalent to modern 你. The scan supports claims about 尔/爾, not the formation of 你.
evidence.title: 字源, 2012, Tianjin Guji Press / Liaoning People’s Publishing House, ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.text: The entry identifies 你 as a second-person singular pronoun, reports that it is absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and Shuowen, cites 集韻·止韻 “你，汝也” and a passage from 隋書·李密傳, and describes later and modern usage. Its cited passage does not establish the date of the wording independently of the text’s transmission.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭 你

evidence.field: 釋義; 集韻 citation and usage examples
evidence.text: Records 顧氏補刊本《集韻·上聲·止韻》 “你，乃里切。汝也,” with a second-person example from 周書 and subsequent plural, possessive, and generic examples. This documents dictionary-reported senses and citations; it does not by itself provide a dated chronology linking those senses.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 你

evidence.field: 尔; 形義通解 and historical examples
evidence.text: The entry describes 尔 (anciently 尒) as formed by taking the upper part of 爾, hence a shortened graphic form; it reports 尔/爾 uses for second-person forms including you/your and cites the Warring States Zhongshan Wang Ding “毋忘尔邦.” It says 尔 later developed into modern 你. This account concerns the word/graph history of 尔; it does not directly establish 尔 as a phonetic component in 你.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭 尔

evidence.field: 尔 / 爾 relationship; simplified counterpart
evidence.text: The 爾 entry indexes 尔 as an alternative form and explicitly identifies 尔 as the simplified character used for 爾. This supports the direction 爾 → 尔 as standardized simplification; it does not classify the component pair in 你, where the visible form is 尔 and origin_form is blank.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 爾

evidence.text: The official character record identifies 你 as U+4F60, gives Mandarin nǐ, and encodes its visible structure as ⿰亻尔. This is contemporary character and reading metadata, not evidence for an ancient phonetic relationship.
evidence.title: 字形資訊 — 你, CNS 11643

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart
evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table, GSR-sorted PDF, entries 尔 and 爾
evidence.text: The 2014 version 1.1 GSR-sorted table gives 尔, gloss ‘you(r),’ Middle Chinese nyeX and Old Chinese *n[ə][r]ʔ. It gives 爾 with multiple entries, including ‘you(r)’ at the same MC/OC values. The PDF search result provided no 你 row, so it cannot establish a within-system 你–尔 comparison. Preserve Baxter–Sagart notation as distinct from Zhengzhang’s system.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014), GSR-sorted table

evidence.source: Local HSK Unihan extract; official Unicode lookup attempted
evidence.text: The local extract gives 你 kMandarin nǐ and 尔 kMandarin ěr. These are local contemporary reading rows only. Official Unicode per-character pages for both code points returned internal errors, so no external Unicode record was verified in this pass.
evidence.title: Unihan database lookup (attempted; inaccessible)

search_audit.outcome: Direct JSONL search yielded no 你 headword passage; supplied candidates are mentions/index material. Personally inspected original-resolution scan of 字源 PDF page 77, printed page 65, including the complete 尔 entry. No suspect OCR span in the cited 尔 prose required correction.

gaps: No relevant 字源 你 headword entry was located in the supplied candidate records. The local scan check was limited to PDF page 77 (printed page 65), the relevant 尔 component entry. PDF page 1100 is a locator hit for 女/姓, not evidence about 你; its supplied OCR includes glyph placeholders but does not bear on claims used here.

No inspected paleographic or dictionary source directly demonstrates whether 你 was formed phonosemantically (亻 semantic + 尔 phonetic) or ideographically (人 + 尔). The phonetic analysis remains a proposal; the present sources do not establish it or a competing construction.

[SCAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED] 字源 PDF page 1100, OCR spans containing [glyph:p001]–[glyph:p009], including the 女/姓 material; it is a locator hit unrelated to the 你 headword and was not inspected in this invocation. Do not use it for 你 evidence.

Official Unicode Unihan pages for U+4F60 and U+5C14 were inaccessible. The checkout has only the tracked HSK extract rows, not sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt or sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; no official external per-character Unihan evidence or exact full local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked.

A matched 你–尔 pronunciation comparison within one historical reconstruction system was not established. The Baxter–Sagart source gives 尔/爾 but no 你 row; a local Zhengzhang value from dossier material is not a substitute for a checked matching component row.

Exact earliest surviving attestation of 你 and dates of the quoted 隋書 wording remain unestablished. MOE and CUHK report dictionary citations and examples, but these do not independently date the text witnesses.
MOE lists plural, possessive, and generic uses without establishing their chronology or semantic transitions from singular ‘you.’
The 尔/爾 entry in 字源 says 爾’s early construction is unclear and provides no analysis of its depiction or object referent. No object-name or borrowing account should be inferred from this passage.
